notes: The mirror image of the LEFT JOIN case, and the reason it is worth having both: a RIGHT JOIN preserves the *right* relation and null-extends the left, so the answers swap. PostgreSQL's planner also rewrites RIGHT JOIN into a LEFT JOIN with the inputs commuted, which means an engine reading nullability out of a plan must follow the swap rather than trusting the textual order of the FROM clause.
